content: Secret-scanning consensus (partially verified via docs.github.com): detection is not remediation; a secret pushed to a remote must be treated as compromised because bots harvest public-commit credentials within minutes; revocation/rotation is the only guaranteed fix; history rewriting (filter-repo/BFG) is hygiene, and clones/forks/platform caches retain the secret regardless. Prevention layers: pre-commit gitleaks protect --staged, CI secret scanning, GitHub push protection (blocks pushes matching known patterns, free on public repos). TruffleHog differentiates live vs dead credentials via provider verification. GitHub docs confirm revoke-first ordering and push-protection availability (verified); bot-harvest timing is vendor-reported (GitGuardian), unverified this run.
